references.text: The following verse in [ref:Luk 20:36|Luke 20:36] explains why those found worthy of the coming age and the resurrection from the dead do not marry – they are like angels and are children of God, being children of the resurrection.

In [ref:Matt 22:30|Matthew 22:30], Jesus gives the same answer to the Sadducees: "In the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels of God in heaven." This is the parallel passage in Matthew.
[ref:Mark 12:25|Mark 12:25] is the parallel passage in Mark, where Jesus says that "when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven."
[ref:2 Tess 1:5|2 Thessalonians 1:5] speaks of being counted worthy (καταξιωθῆναι) for God's kingdom – the same expression used in Luke 20:35 about being found worthy of the coming age.

In [ref:Fil 3:11|Philippians 3:11], Paul expresses his hope to attain the resurrection from the dead (τὴν ἐξανάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν), a parallel to the expression "the resurrection from the dead" in this verse.
[ref:Åp 3:4|Revelation 3:4] refers to those who are worthy (ἄξιοι) – they will walk with Christ in white. The idea of being found worthy to share in the coming life is a parallel to Luke 20:35.

In [ref:Apg 5:41|Acts 5:41], the apostles rejoice at being counted worthy (κατηξιώθησαν) to suffer disgrace for the Name's sake. The word "kaταξιόω" (to be counted worthy) is the same as that used for being found worthy of the coming age.

[ref:Dan 12:2-3|Daniel 12:2–3] is a central Old Testament text about the resurrection from the dead, where some awake to eternal life and others to shame. Those deemed worthy of the resurrection to life are parallel to those mentioned in Luke 20:35.

In [ref:Heb 11:35|Hebrews 11:35], it is said that some refused release so as to obtain a better resurrection – the idea of being found worthy to share in the resurrection from the dead is closely connected to this.
